## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best wind. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best wind direction.
- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.

| Variable | Research confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Swell direction | High | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Swell size | Moderate | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a surf magazine. |
| Swell period | Low | Supported by one source (a forecast site's spot guide). |
| Wind | Low | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a surf magazine; 1 disagrees. |
| Tide | Low | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a surf magazine; 2 disagree. |
| Bottom / bathymetry | Moderate | Described by 2 independent sources, including a community source. |
| Season | Moderate | Supported by 5 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| How the wave breaks | High | Described by 5 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Wind, previously unsupported, now has readable support near the profile's 60 deg: east (Surf Atlas, 'E trade winds coming straight offshore'), northeast (Yeeew), SE to NE (Indonesian Surf Guide, midpoint E) and SE, NE (Lineup); Surf-Forecast's ESE (112.5 deg) stays the outlier. Lineup's text closely mirrors Indonesian Surf Guide and may be derived from it. Tide: all tides (WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, Yeeew, Lineup), with the left working through the tide and the right needing mid to high tide; Surf-Forecast says high and Kala Surf says mid-high. The profile's 'all' is well supported. Swell direction: SW (Surf-Forecast, Surf Atlas), S-SW (Indonesian Surf Guide), S (Yeeew), inside the profile window. Size: WannaSurf 3-5 ft start, holds 8 ft+; Indonesian Surf Guide and Yeeew waist high to double overhead (about 3-12 ft faces, an approximate conversion), consistent with the profile's 3-10 ft. Period: only 'groundswells more frequent than windswells' (Surf-Forecast); no numbers found. Season: May-October (Surf-Forecast, Surf Atlas), June-September (WannaSurf, Kala), April-October (Lineup), all inside the profile. Wave direction: an A-frame with a left and a right (Indonesian Surf Guide, Surf Atlas, WannaSurf, Surf-Forecast), supporting 'both'; indonesia.travel's 'waves sweep to the left' is about Lakey Beach in general. Kala Surf's wind lines contradict each other, so no wind was recorded from it. Surfer Today still 403. No peer-reviewed, survey or official source found.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 3–5 ft | documented | S2 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | waist high to double overhead | documented | S4, S6 | no separate setting; working range 3–10 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 8 ft | documented | S2 | `wave_height_max_ft` 10 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft (the page's own conversion; face or offshore height not stated).
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 2.5m+ / 8ft+”
- **Ideal range**: The Indonesian Surf Guide gives the wave size as waist high to 2x overhead and Yeeew says it gets good between waist high and double overhead; both are face heights relative to the surfer, with no number in feet.
  - S4 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Wave size | waist high – 2x overhead”
  - S6 (Yeeew!): “Gets good between waist high and double overhead.”
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf's top bracket is 2.5 m+ / 8 ft+, an open-ended bound (scale not stated); no excerpt gives a true upper limit.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 2.5m+ / 8ft+”

Notes:

- **Break type**: Surf-Forecast says the reef gives lefts and rights, the Indonesian Surf Guide calls it a genuine A-frame with a left and a right off the same peak, Surfer Today (search summary) a picturesque A-frame, and Surf Atlas describes long lefts and short, fast rights.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “Reef breaks provide lefts and rights.”
  - S4 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Lakey Peak is one of the best genuine A-frames in the world, with a left and a right of the same peak.”
  - S3 (Surfer Today): “Lakey Peak is described as a picturesque A-frame”
  - S5 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “Long lefts that curl into the reef channel. Short, fast rights that barrel like clockwork.”
- **Orientation**: Surf Atlas says the reef points head-on into the SW swell channel; no bearing beyond SW is given.
  - S5 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “point head-on into the SW swell channel”
- **Exposure**: No excerpt describes the break's geographic exposure.
- **Bathymetry**: WannaSurf gives a coral reef bottom with sand and the Indonesian Surf Guide says the reef can get very shallow on the low tide and is sharp; no survey is cited.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “BottomReef (coral,sharp rocks etc..) with sand”
  - S4 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “The reef can get very shallow on the low tide and is sharp so be aware.”

## Conflicting information

- **Wind · offshore**: Surf Atlas says east trade winds come straight offshore and the Indonesian Surf Guide and Lineup give SE to NE as best (centred on east), while Yeeew gives northeast (45 deg) as best and Surf-Forecast east-southeast (112.5 deg) as offshore; NE and ESE are 67.5 deg apart.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: WannaSurf, the Indonesian Surf Guide, Yeeew and Lineup say it works on all tides, with the right needing mid to higher tides, while Surf-Forecast says best around high tide and Kala Surf that high and mid tides tend to be best.
